title: GREEN impl: NEW harness/state_reconciler.py exposing state_reconcile_lock; brief_reaper wraps its move under it
acceptance_criteria: NEW file harness/state_reconciler.py is created via whole-file __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ (this is the file-creating leaf).
harness/state_reconciler.py exposes state_reconcile_lock(state_dir) as a context manager that acquires and releases the single dedicated lock file state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock.
state_reconcile_lock is distinct from git_commit.lock: it never opens, acquires, or releases state_dir/control/autowork/git_commit.lock.
tools/brief_reaper.py is edited additively to wrap its archive move in `with state_reconcile_lock(state_dir):`, deriving state_dir as <repo_root>/state.
The slow destructive (move) section runs under state_reconcile_lock and NEVER under git_commit.lock; behavior is fail-closed and the reaper stays fully fail-safe (returns [] on any error).
The oracle test file tests/harness/test_state_reconcile_lock.py is GREEN after this lands.

spec.objective: Create the NEW harness/state_reconciler.py and the single shared serialization primitive state_reconcile_lock(state_dir), then make tools/brief_reaper.py acquire that shared lock around its move — turning the oracle GREEN while honoring the ONE-SHARED-LOCK invariant.
functional_requirements: Create harness/state_reconciler.py via a whole-file __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ defining a @contextmanager state_reconcile_lock(state_dir) that opens/creates state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock (mkdir parents exist_ok), takes an exclusive fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX), yields, and releases (LOCK_UN + close) in a finally so two callers serialize on this ONE dedicated lock.

state_reconcile_lock is distinct from git_commit.lock: it only ever touches state_reconcile.lock and never opens/acquires/releases git_commit.lock, so a slow destructive section held under it leaves git_commit.lock free.

Edit tools/brief_reaper.py additively so its archive move (the _move_no_clobber calls / dest mkdir + moves) runs inside `with state_reconcile_lock(state_dir):`, importing state_reconcile_lock from harness.state_reconciler and computing state_dir = root / 'state'.

Keep the reaper fully fail-safe and fail-closed: lock acquisition or release errors are contained so reap_for_task still returns [] on any unexpected error and never raises; the move section is never run under git_commit.lock.
spec.interfaces: state_reconcile_lock(state_dir) -> context manager acquiring/releasing the single dedicated state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock (in harness/state_reconciler.py); distinct from git_commit.lock; the slow destructive section is held under it but NEVER under git_commit.lock. tools/brief_reaper.py wraps its move in `with state_reconcile_lock(state_dir):`.
edge_cases: fcntl unavailable: import it in-body and degrade so the context manager still yields (best-effort advisory lock) without raising, matching the daemon's in-body fcntl convention.
state_dir or control/autowork/ missing: create parents with mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) before opening the lock file.
Exception raised inside the `with` body: the lock is still released in a finally (LOCK_UN + close) so a later mutator can acquire it.
brief_reaper called when archive=False or when nothing matches: the lock wrap must not change the existing early-return behavior and must never strand the source (MOVE NEVER DELETE).
Must never raw-edit git_commit.lock or any semantic marker; the lock file is created/locked via os.open + fcntl only.
non_goals: integration: NO live-daemon run; correctness is proven by the hermetic oracle, not an end-to-end daemon drive.
Does NOT implement classify_product, the discriminators, cleanup_state, disk reapers, prepare_workspace, or any status logic — ONLY the lock primitive plus the reaper's acquisition of it.
Does NOT acquire or hold git_commit.lock across the slow section; does NOT use git mv; does NOT rewrite brief bytes or touch brief mtime.
Does NOT raw-edit a semantic marker (pause/full_stop/inactivity_escalated.json/live allowlist/git_commit.lock) and does NOT flip the autowork.state_reconcile flag.
spec.implementation_notes: Model the lock-file location and fcntl usage on harness/autowork_daemon.py:_acquire_commit_lock_or_reclaim (state_dir/control/autowork/<name>.lock, in-body `import fcntl`, os.open(O_RDWR|O_CREAT, 0o644)). state_reconcile_lock should be a simple blocking @contextmanager (from contextlib) yielding after LOCK_EX and releasing in finally — the slow op runs inside it but it must never touch git_commit.lock. In tools/brief_reaper.py, add `from harness.state_reconciler import state_reconcile_lock` (local/top-level import) and wrap only the move/dest-creation block (lines that mkdir dest and call _move_no_clobber) in `with state_reconcile_lock(root / 'state'):`, leaving the ground-truth integration checks above it unchanged. Whole-file harness/state_reconciler.py via __JANUSMASK_MANIFEST__ (file-creating leaf); brief_reaper edit is additive.
